CLINICAL INDICATION:
Groin pain / palpable bulge; rule out femoral hernia.
TECHNIQUE:

High-frequency linear (7–15 MHz) grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound of the bilateral inguinal canals, Hesselbach triangles, and femoral canals was performed at rest and during dynamic Valsalva maneuvers in both supine and upright/standing positions.
FINDINGS:
Right Femoral Region:
Location: No herniation is seen medial to the common femoral vein below the inguinal ligament during Valsalva.
Fascial Defect & Sac: No femoral ring defect or hernia sac.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Femoral Vessels: The right common femoral artery and vein are patent and compressible.
Left Femoral Region:
Location: Normal left femoral canal without hernia.
Fascial Defect & Sac: No femoral ring defect or hernia sac.
Reducibility & Viability: Not applicable (no hernia identified).
Femoral Vessels: Common femoral vein demonstrates normal compressibility and respiratory phasicity.
Soft Tissues & Lymph Nodes:
Scattered normal-appearing, oval reactive inguinal lymph nodes with preserved fatty hila measuring up to 1.1 cm in long axis. No soft tissue mass or fluid collection.
IMPRESSION:
No sonographic evidence of a right or left femoral hernia at rest or during provocative Valsalva maneuvers.

subs.title: Femoral Hernia (Classic / Incarcerated)
items: Located inferior to the inguinal ligament and medial to the common femoral vein, there is a narrow fascial defect measuring [X.X] cm through which a hernia sac measuring [X.X] x [X.X] cm protrudes, compressing the medial wall of the common femoral vein during Valsalva. The sac contains [non-reducible omental fat / an incarcerated small bowel loop].

subs.title: Strangulated Groin Hernia (Surgical Emergency)
items: Strangulation Alert: Within the [right / left] [indirect inguinal / direct inguinal / femoral] hernia sac, there is a fixed, non-reducible loop of fluid-distended, thick-walled small bowel (wall thickness [X.X] mm) accompanied by anechoic/complex fluid within the hernia sac and absent intramural color Doppler blood flow, diagnostic of a strangulated hernia.

bank.title: PART 2: EXAMPLE FINDINGS FROM THE SAMPLE ABNORMAL REPORT
items: Femoral Canal & Vessels: Inferior to the left inguinal ligament and immediately medial to the left common femoral vein, there is a narrow 1.0 cm femoral ring defect through which an incarcerated left femoral hernia sac measuring 2.6 x 1.9 cm protrudes, causing mild extrinsic compression of the adjacent common femoral vein during Valsalva. The sac contains non-reducible, mildly edematous extraperitoneal fat with preserved internal Doppler vascularity and no bowel loops.
Incarcerated left femoral hernia (neck width 1.0 cm, sac 2.6 cm) containing non-reducible extraperitoneal fat without bowel involvement or signs of strangulation.

bank.title: PART 3: NORMAL PHRASES
items: Femoral Canal & Vessels: The right common femoral artery and vein are patent and compressible. No herniation is seen medial to the common femoral vein below the inguinal ligament during Valsalva.
